title: Did a U.S. Boat Strike Amount to a War Crime?

sentences.zh: 我凌晨4点半给总统打了电话，他接听了。

sentences.zh: 七十年的太空探索。

sentences.en: We want to see what's beyond the next star.
sentences.zh: 我们想看看下一颗恒星之外有什么。

sentences.en: The New York Times, celebrating 175 years of helping you understand the world and make the most of each day.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》，庆祝175年来致力于帮助您了解世界并充分利用每一天。

sentences.en: Subscribe now for a special offer at nytimes.com slash subscribe.
sentences.zh: 立即订阅，获取nytimes.com/subscribe上的特别优惠。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Rachel Abrams, and this is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的瑞秋·艾布拉姆斯，这是《每日新闻》节目。

sentences.en: It's been three months since the American military began firing on boats from South America, killing more than 80 people and prompting Democrats to raise urgent questions
sentences.zh: 美军开始向南美船只开火已经三个月了，造成80多人死亡，并促使民主党人提出紧急质疑，

sentences.en: about whether these attacks might be illegal.
sentences.zh: 质疑这些袭击是否可能违法。

sentences.en: But now...
sentences.zh: 但现在……

sentences.en: We're going to conduct oversight and we're going to try to get to the facts.
sentences.zh: 我们将进行监督，并努力查明事实。

sentences.en: New questions about one of those operations in which the military killed survivors with a second missile have prompted congressional Republicans
sentences.zh: 关于其中一次行动的新质疑——军方用第二枚导弹杀死了幸存者——促使国会共和党人

sentences.en: to join those calls for accountability.
sentences.zh: 加入到这些追责的呼声中。

sentences.en: There are very serious concerns in Congress about the attacks on the so-called drug boats down in the Caribbean.
sentences.zh: 国会对加勒比海地区针对所谓“毒品船”的袭击存在非常严重的关切。

sentences.en: Today, my colleague Charlie Savage explains the renewed debate and how the administration is justifying its actions.
sentences.zh: 今天，我的同事查理·萨维奇将解释这场重新引发的辩论，以及政府如何为其行动辩护。

sentences.en: It's Wednesday, December 3rd.
sentences.zh: 今天是12月3日，星期三。

sentences.en: Charlie, we had you on the show a couple months ago to talk about the Trump administration's campaign of boat strikes in the Caribbean
sentences.zh: 查理，几个月前你曾做客我们的节目，谈论特朗普政府在加勒比海发起的船只打击行动，

sentences.en: against boats that they argued were carrying drugs from Venezuela to the United States.
sentences.zh: 针对的是他们声称从委内瑞拉向美国运送毒品的船只。

sentences.en: And from the beginning, there were questions about the legality of these attacks.
sentences.zh: 从一开始，人们就对这些袭击的合法性存有疑问。

sentences.en: And those questions took on new urgency this week with lawmakers, notably Republicans, announcing plans to investigate.
sentences.zh: 本周，随着立法者（特别是共和党人）宣布调查计划，这些疑问变得更加紧迫。

sentences.en: And that's where I'd like to start today with the Washington Post story that seems to have kicked all of this off.
sentences.zh: 这就是我今天想从《华盛顿邮报》那篇似乎引发了这一切的报道开始谈起的原因。

sentences.en: So the day after Thanksgiving, the Washington Post published a very good story about the first of Trump's boat attacks way back on September 2nd.
sentences.zh: 感恩节后的第二天，《华盛顿邮报》发表了一篇非常出色的报道，讲述了特朗普早在9月2日发起的第一次船只袭击。

sentences.en: Now, that had always been the most questionable of the 21 attacks that have happened so far.
sentences.zh: 那一直是迄今为止发生的21次袭击中最令人质疑的一次。

sentences.en: And part of the reason for that is that there were some additional complicating details that had come to light in September, including that the boat had turned around
sentences.zh: 部分原因是9月份曝光了一些额外的复杂细节，包括船只在被袭击前已经掉头，

sentences.en: before it had attacked, that there were more missile strikes on the boat before it sank than just the one that was shown in a video that Trump had put out.
sentences.zh: 以及在沉没前，船只遭受的导弹袭击次数比特朗普发布视频中显示的要多。

sentences.en: And The Intercept had reported that there were initial survivors of the first missile strike that died in the subsequent strike.
sentences.zh: 《拦截》杂志报道称，第一枚导弹袭击后的初期幸存者在随后的袭击中丧生。

sentences.en: But that was all kind of bare bones.
sentences.zh: 但这些都还只是粗略的情况。

sentences.en: This new story added significant and rich detail about this strike.
sentences.zh: 这篇新报道为这次袭击增添了重要且丰富的细节。

sentences.en: And among the other things it reported was that Admiral Frank Bradley, who was running the operation, had ordered the second strike to kill the survivors of the first one
sentences.zh: 报道中提到的其他内容包括：负责此次行动的弗兰克·布拉德利海军上将下令进行第二次打击，以杀死第一次袭击的幸存者，

sentences.en: because Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth had said to kill everyone.
sentences.zh: 因为国防部长皮特·海格塞斯下令“杀光所有人”。

sentences.en: And this set off a furor that had not happened back in September when the basic outlines of these facts had first come to light.
sentences.zh: 这引发了一场骚动，而9月份这些事实的基本轮廓首次曝光时，并没有出现这种情况。

sentences.en: So explain that for a second, Charlie.
sentences.zh: 查理，请解释一下这一点。

sentences.en: Why is it that this is now producing this kind of bipartisan outrage?
sentences.zh: 为什么现在会引发这种两党共愤？

sentences.en: So to understand that, I think you have to work through the administration's explanation of what it's doing.
sentences.zh: 要理解这一点，我认为你必须梳理一下政府对自己行为的解释。

sentences.en: the administration has put forward a legal theory that this is an armed conflict.
sentences.zh: 政府提出了一种法律理论，即这是一场武装冲突。

sentences.en: This is a war that Trump has decided we're at war, even though Congress has not authorized one, a war with drug
sentences.zh: 这是一场战争，特朗普决定我们处于战争状态，尽管国会并未授权，这是一场与贩毒

sentences.en: cartels, and that the people on the boat smuggling these drugs, supposedly for the drug cartels, are not criminals.
sentences.zh: 集团的战争，而船上那些据称是为贩毒集团走私毒品的人不是罪犯。

sentences.en: They are combatants.
sentences.zh: 他们是战斗人员。

sentences.en: And a lot of people do not think that is a legitimate interpretation of the law and think this is not an armed conflict.
sentences.zh: 许多人认为这不是对法律的合法解释，并认为这并非武装冲突。

sentences.en: But even if you accept it under the laws of armed conflict very explicitly, you cannot fire upon people who are out of the
sentences.zh: 但即使你接受这一点，根据武装冲突法，你绝对不能向那些已经退出

sentences.en: fight, people who have surrendered, people who are incredibly wounded and unable to fight you back, or explicitly shipwrecked sailors cannot be fired upon.
sentences.zh: 战斗的人开火，不能向投降的人、受重伤无法还击的人开火，或者明确禁止向遇难船只的船员开火。

sentences.en: That is a war crime.
sentences.zh: 那是战争罪。

sentences.en: So based on what you just outlined, this first strike in September that destroys the boat, kills most of the people, but leaves a couple of survivors,
sentences.zh: 所以根据你刚才概述的情况，9月份的那次首次打击摧毁了船只，杀死了大部分人，但留下了几名幸存者，

sentences.en: that second strike that kills the remaining survivors because of the rules of war about not striking people that basically pose no imminent threat to you seems illegal on its face.
sentences.zh: 而那第二次打击杀死了剩余的幸存者，鉴于战争规则中关于不得打击基本不对你构成迫在眉睫威胁的人的规定，这看起来显然是非法的。

sentences.en: And that is why this Washington Post story catches everybody's attention.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么《华盛顿邮报》的这篇报道引起了所有人的注意。

sentences.en: What exactly do we know, though, about what Hegseth did or did not do in relation to that September 2nd strike?
sentences.zh: 不过，关于海格塞斯在9月2日那次袭击中做了什么或没做什么，我们到底了解多少？

sentences.en: Like, what do we know about the order he gave?
sentences.zh: 比如，我们对他的命令了解多少？

sentences.en: So Hegseth has acknowledged from the beginning that he authorized a lethal strike on this boat.
sentences.zh: 海格塞斯从一开始就承认他授权对这艘船进行了致命打击。

sentences.en: This was not a capture operation.
sentences.zh: 这不是一次抓捕行动。

sentences.en: They weren't aiming to disable the engines and then go arrest the guys.
sentences.zh: 他们的目的不是瘫痪引擎然后去逮捕那些人。

sentences.en: The aim was to kill the people on the boat, sink the boat, destroy the purported drugs on the boat.
sentences.zh: 目的是杀死船上的人，击沉船只，销毁船上所谓的毒品。

sentences.en: So that's not in dispute.
sentences.zh: 所以这一点没有争议。

sentences.en: But the question is whether the orders he gave contemplated that the first missile wouldn't accomplish all those things and that there might be shipwrecked survivors.
sentences.zh: 但问题在于，他下达的命令是否预见到第一枚导弹可能无法完成所有这些目标，并且可能会有遇难幸存者。

sentences.en: And if that happened, should they be killed too?
sentences.zh: 如果发生了这种情况，他们是否也应该被杀死？

sentences.en: Or was the order silent on that possibility?
sentences.zh: 还是说命令对这种可能性保持沉默？

sentences.en: But whatever was in those orders, we have been told that Hegseth gave no additional instructions to Bradley once the attack commenced.
sentences.zh: 但无论命令中写了什么，我们被告知，一旦袭击开始，海格塞斯没有给布拉德利任何额外的指示。

sentences.en: In other words, he didn't see or hear that there were initial survivors and then say something.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，他没有看到或听到有初期幸存者，然后说了什么。

sentences.en: But this is something Congress needs to figure out.
sentences.zh: 但这正是国会需要弄清楚的事情。

sentences.en: And regardless of what Hegseth said or intended, the next question is, what did Admiral Bradley understand his orders to be?
sentences.zh: 而且无论海格塞斯说了什么或意图如何，下一个问题是，布拉德利海军上将如何理解他的命令？

sentences.en: Is his intent, we want to kill those two people?
sentences.zh: 他的意图是“我们要杀死那两个人”吗？

sentences.en: Does he say anything that leaves a contemporaneous record that would explain whether he thought he was specifically trying to kill shipwrecked survivors or was just hitting what he thought was a lawful target again?
sentences.zh: 他是否说了什么留下了即时记录，可以解释他认为自己是在专门试图杀死遇难幸存者，还是仅仅在再次打击他认为合法的目标？

sentences.en: then this starts to get kind of esoteric because what difference does it make if his intent was to
sentences.zh: 然后这开始变得有些深奥了，因为如果他的意图是

sentences.en: specifically kill these people versus destroy the vessel if the same missile is hitting the same
sentences.zh: 专门杀死这些人，而不是摧毁船只，这有什么区别呢？如果同一枚导弹击中了同一个

sentences.en: object causing the same damage regardless and this is part of the reason why trying to apply
sentences.zh: 目标，造成了同样的损害，无论如何，这就是为什么试图将

sentences.en: the laws of armed conflict to this situation starts to become very unsatisfactory because
sentences.zh: 武装冲突法应用于这种情况开始变得非常令人不满的原因，因为

sentences.en: these rules are written for naval engagements between warships of nation states that have guns that are flying colors.
sentences.zh: 这些规则是为民族国家军舰之间悬挂旗帜的交战而编写的。

sentences.en: And if a ship wants to surrender, it can lower its colors and stop firing its guns and then it's out of the fight.
sentences.zh: 如果一艘船想要投降，它可以降下旗帜并停止开火，然后它就退出了战斗。

sentences.en: But this is not a warship.
sentences.zh: 但这并不是一艘军舰。

sentences.en: This is a speedboat that may or may not be carrying an illicit consumer product.
sentences.zh: 这是一艘可能载有也可能没载非法消费品的快艇。

sentences.en: So basically what you're saying is that if the intent here from Bradley was to simply kill the
sentences.zh: 所以你基本上是说，如果布拉德利的意图仅仅是杀死

sentences.en: two remaining survivors, it would be really pretty clear cut what he had done and whether it was legal in terms of the laws of war.
sentences.zh: 剩下的两名幸存者，那么他所做的事情以及这在战争法方面是否合法，就会非常清楚了。

sentences.en: But if he was aiming to sink the boat or destroy the drugs, which was also part of the initial mandate and order from Hegseth, that's where it gets a bit murkier, right?
sentences.zh: 但如果他的目标是击沉船只或销毁毒品（这也是海格塞斯最初授权和命令的一部分），那情况就变得有些模糊了，对吧？

sentences.en: That's where it gets murkier.
sentences.zh: 这就是变得模糊的地方。

sentences.en: Of course, even for that initial order to be lawful, this has to be an armed conflict, which very, very few people outside of the administration think it is.
sentences.zh: 当然，即使是最初的命令要合法，这也必须是一场武装冲突，而政府之外极少有人认为这是武装冲突。

sentences.en: And so if it's not an armed conflict, the first missile was murder.
sentences.zh: 所以如果这不是武装冲突，第一枚导弹就是谋杀。

sentences.en: The second missile was murder.
sentences.zh: 第二枚导弹也是谋杀。

sentences.en: They were all unlawful.
sentences.zh: 它们都是非法的。

sentences.en: How has the administration responded so far?
sentences.zh: 政府到目前为止是如何回应的？

sentences.en: The administration as a whole has defended the entire operation.
sentences.zh: 政府整体上为整个行动进行了辩护。

sentences.en: It is stressed that Hegseth did not specifically order the killing of the two initial survivors and has suggested that that is a misinterpretation of what happened.
sentences.zh: 它强调海格塞斯并没有专门下令杀死那两名初期幸存者，并暗示那是对所发生事件的误读。

sentences.en: Nevertheless, it has defended the actions of Admiral Bradley in ordering the follow-up strike, insisting it was lawful.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，它还是为布拉德利海军上将下令进行后续打击的行为进行了辩护，坚称这是合法的。

sentences.en: And that's the administration as a whole.
sentences.zh: 这就是政府整体的态度。

sentences.en: That said, very interestingly, on Sunday night, if there were a second strike that killed people...
sentences.zh: 话虽如此，非常有趣的是，在周日晚上，如果确实有第二次打击杀死了人……

sentences.en: President Trump was asked about this by reporters, and he distanced himself from the second strike.
sentences.zh: 特朗普总统被记者问及此事，他与第二次打击保持了距离。

sentences.en: No, I wouldn't have wanted that, not a second strike.
sentences.zh: 不，我不会想要那样，不是第二次打击。

sentences.en: The first strike was very lethal.
sentences.zh: 第一次打击非常致命。

sentences.en: It was fine.
sentences.zh: 那很好。

sentences.en: If there were two people around, but Pete said that didn't happen.
sentences.zh: 如果周围有两个人，但皮特说那并没有发生。

sentences.en: Does that make you...
sentences.zh: 这让你……

sentences.en: I have great confidence.
sentences.zh: 我非常有信心。

sentences.en: He said the first one was fine, including the fact that it was lethal, but he wouldn't have wanted the second one.
sentences.zh: 他说第一次打击很好，包括它是致命的事实，但他不会想要第二次打击。

sentences.en: Why not?
sentences.zh: 为什么不呢？

sentences.en: And he said the suggestion is he has some kind of discomfort with that follow-up strike.
sentences.zh: 他说这暗示了他对那次后续打击感到某种不安。

sentences.en: This all makes me wonder how this sort of thing would normally work.
sentences.zh: 这一切让我好奇这种事情通常是如何运作的。

sentences.en: Like, the legality of these strikes in this kind of detail is the thing at issue.
sentences.zh: 比如，这些打击在细节上的合法性才是问题的关键。

sentences.en: And so I'm curious about who is advising the people involved, like Commander Bradley or Pete Hegseth, about what is legal and what is not in the moment?
sentences.zh: 所以我很好奇是谁在建议相关人员，比如布拉德利指挥官或皮特·海格塞斯，关于在当时什么是合法的，什么不是？

sentences.en: Well, the way it's supposed to work is the military commanders at each level of the chain are supposed to have staff judge advocate general officers, JAGs,
sentences.zh: 嗯，按照预想的运作方式，指挥链中每一级的军事指挥官都应该有参谋军法官（JAGs），

sentences.en: who are advising them about the laws of war and what would cross the line.
sentences.zh: 他们会就战争法以及什么会越界向他们提供建议。

sentences.en: And Pete Exeth has a general counsel and is part of an administration that is advised by the Justice Department.
sentences.zh: 皮特·海格塞斯有一位总法律顾问，并且他所在的政府由司法部提供建议。

sentences.en: But one of the things we know about this operation as it was getting put together in July, August, early September, leading up to this initial attack,
sentences.zh: 但我们所知道的关于这次行动的一件事是，在7月、8月、9月初，在导致这次最初袭击的过程中，

sentences.en: is that the deliberations were very closely held and that few career military lawyers were allowed into the room.
sentences.zh: 审议过程非常保密，很少有职业军事律师被允许进入房间。

sentences.en: There weren't a lot of lawyers, uniform lawyers, non-politically appointed lawyers, being allowed into the deliberations.
sentences.zh: 没有多少律师，穿制服的律师，非政治任命的律师被允许参与审议。

sentences.en: Pete Hegseth comes up as a platoon leader in war, not a senior commander, and he seems to have acquired a hostility towards the idea of military lawyers.
sentences.zh: 皮特·海格塞斯是作为战争中的排长出身，而不是高级指挥官，他似乎对军事律师的概念产生了敌意。

sentences.en: He talks about them as jag-offs in his memoir.
sentences.zh: 他在回忆录中称他们为“jag-offs”（混蛋）。

sentences.en: He seems to blame them for rules of engagement that he found to be unduly restrictive about when his troops could open fire on someone they saw as a threat.
sentences.zh: 他似乎将他认为过分限制其部队何时可以向他视为威胁的人开火的交战规则归咎于他们。

sentences.en: And he seems to misunderstand that the jags are not the ones setting those rules.
sentences.zh: 他似乎误解了，制定这些规则的并不是军法官。

sentences.en: The commanders are.
sentences.zh: 而是指挥官。

sentences.en: And he acquires from that this hostility.
sentences.zh: 他由此产生了这种敌意。

sentences.en: And the first thing he does is he fires the top jags of the services.
sentences.zh: 他做的第一件事就是解雇了各军种的顶级军法官。

sentences.en: You know, he's been trying to replace them with not career active duty JAGs that have come up through the JAG Corps,
sentences.zh: 你知道，他一直试图用那些不是通过军法官体系成长起来的职业现役军法官来取代他们，

sentences.en: but with National Guardsmen who are sort of more political officials coming out of states.
sentences.zh: 而是用来自各州的、更具政治色彩的国民警卫队官员来取代。

sentences.en: So, Charlie, what would the legal rationale be for Bradley to order that second strike?
sentences.zh: 那么，查理，布拉德利下令进行第二次打击的法律依据是什么？

sentences.en: Like, what would that be based on?
sentences.zh: 比如，那会基于什么？

sentences.en: It's hard to answer not knowing the details of the sort of questions that we've been talking about that remain fuzzy.
sentences.zh: 在不知道我们一直在谈论的那些仍然模糊的问题的细节的情况下，很难回答。

sentences.en: And one of the issues here that listeners ought to understand is that we now know that behind the scenes, a couple days after this strike,
sentences.zh: 听众应该了解的一个问题是，我们现在知道在幕后，在那次打击几天后，

sentences.en: the Justice Department's Office of Legal Counsel, which is a very powerful node in the executive branch legal system,
sentences.zh: 司法部的法律顾问办公室——这是行政部门法律体系中一个非常有权力的节点——

sentences.en: produced or signed a memo that said it accepted Trump's determination that this is an armed conflict against these drug cartels.
sentences.zh: 起草或签署了一份备忘录，称其接受特朗普关于这是一场针对这些贩毒集团的武装冲突的认定，

sentences.en: and that all this stuff was lawful.
sentences.zh: 并且所有这些事情都是合法的。

sentences.en: And part of the public justification of all this has been, how is it that the cartels are attacking us?
sentences.zh: 而所有这一切的公开辩护的一部分一直是：贩毒集团是如何攻击我们的？

sentences.en: They're not attacking us.
sentences.zh: 他们并没有攻击我们。

sentences.en: They're selling an illicit consumer product.
sentences.zh: 他们是在销售一种非法消费品。

sentences.en: That's bad, but it's not an armed attack on us.
sentences.zh: 那很糟糕，但那不是对我们的武装攻击。

sentences.en: And the rhetorical justification has been, yes, but tens of thousands of Americans are dying from overdoses each year.
sentences.zh: 而修辞上的辩护一直是：是的，但每年有成千上万的美国人死于吸毒过量。

sentences.en: And that's equivalent to an attack.
sentences.zh: 这等同于一次攻击。

sentences.en: So once it's an armed conflict, you can hit the boat, supposedly.
sentences.zh: 所以一旦这是一场武装冲突，你就可以打击那艘船，据称如此。

sentences.en: One of the things that this memo says that is different than the public rhetoric the administration has been putting forward is that the drugs,
sentences.zh: 这份备忘录中与政府提出的公开言论不同的一点是，毒品，

sentences.en: the purported cargo on these boats is a lawful military target.
sentences.zh: 这些船上所谓的货物，是一个合法的军事目标。

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: Because the drug cartels could sell those drugs, they could get the profits and spend them on military equipment to sustain their supposed war efforts against the United States.
sentences.zh: 因为贩毒集团可以出售这些毒品，他们可以获得利润并将其用于购买军事装备，以维持他们所谓的针对美国的战争努力。

sentences.en: And so part of this murkiness around what is the reason the U.S.
sentences.zh: 所以，围绕美国为何在第一时间

sentences.en: fires on this boat in the first instance, keeps firing on it until everyone is dead, them, the boat is at the bottom of the ocean, is was the target of those follow-up strikes
sentences.zh: 向这艘船开火，并持续开火直到所有人死亡、船沉入海底的这种模糊性的一部分是：那些后续打击的目标是

sentences.en: especially?
sentences.zh: 专门针对什么的？

sentences.en: Was it the drugs?
sentences.zh: 是毒品吗？

sentences.en: Was it the boat?
sentences.zh: 是船吗？

sentences.en: Or was it the people?
sentences.zh: 还是人？

sentences.en: Was it all of them in some confusing way?
sentences.zh: 还是以某种令人困惑的方式涵盖了所有这些？

sentences.en: Because if Commander Bradley did that second strike in order to target the drugs on the boat and the killing of the two survivors was collateral damage, then theoretically that
sentences.zh: 因为如果布拉德利指挥官进行第二次打击是为了瞄准船上的毒品，而杀死两名幸存者是附带损害，那么理论上，

sentences.en: could be a defense under what the DOJ laid out as kosher, right?
sentences.zh: 这可以作为司法部所设定的“合规”范围内的辩护，对吧？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Admiral Bradley is in a much stronger position if that's what he says and if there's contemporaneous evidence backing him up.
sentences.zh: 如果布拉德利海军上将这样说，并且有即时证据支持他，那么他的处境会强得多。

sentences.en: Again, though, only if you accept in the first place that this is an armed conflict and this is the right lens to be bringing to bear on this at all.
sentences.zh: 不过，再次强调，前提是你首先接受这是一场武装冲突，并且这是看待此事的正确视角。

sentences.en: Because if it's not, they didn't have a right to kill the people in the first place.
sentences.zh: 因为如果不是，他们一开始就没有权利杀死这些人。

sentences.en: It sounds like there are compelling reasons why the killing of the survivors of that initial strike could be a war crime if the intent was to kill them, which we do not know.
sentences.zh: 听起来确实有充分的理由认为，如果最初那次打击的幸存者是被蓄意杀害的，那么这种行为可能构成战争罪，尽管我们目前还不知道当时是否有这种意图。

sentences.en: And in fact, there is so much that we don't know that we cannot say it sounds like anything definitively.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我们不知道的事情太多了，以至于我们无法断言这听起来像是什么。

sentences.en: And because of that, I am reminded of the video that those six Democratic lawmakers released a couple weeks ago, which urged service members to ignore illegal orders.
sentences.zh: 正因如此，我想起了那六位民主党议员几周前发布的视频，他们敦促军人无视非法命令。

sentences.en: Given everything that we've discussed, how are service members supposed to understand what is legal and what is not.
sentences.zh: 鉴于我们讨论的所有情况，军人该如何理解什么是合法的，什么是不合法的呢？

sentences.en: It is an extremely difficult dilemma when you're faced with a commander-in-chief who's issuing orders backed by a Justice Department memo
sentences.zh: 当你面对一位三军统帅，而他发布的命令背后又有司法部备忘录作为支撑时，这确实是一个极其困难的困境，

sentences.en: that very few people outside of the current executive branch of government think holds water.
sentences.zh: 尽管现任行政部门之外几乎没几个人认为那份备忘录站得住脚。

sentences.en: What are soldiers supposed to do?
sentences.zh: 士兵们该怎么办？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And just to be clear, when the lawmakers made that video,
sentences.zh: 需要明确的是，当议员们制作那个视频时，

sentences.en: Were they aware of any of this?
sentences.zh: 他们知道这些情况吗？

sentences.en: Were they talking about this?
sentences.zh: 他们在讨论这件事吗？

sentences.en: So one of the interesting things about that video from those lawmakers who are all military intelligence veterans telling soldiers you should not obey illegal orders is they don't say what illegal orders they have in mind.
sentences.zh: 关于那些身为军事情报老兵的议员们发布的视频，有趣的一点是，他们告诉士兵不应服从非法命令，但他们并没有说明他们指的是哪些非法命令。

sentences.en: So one of the complaints actually by the Trump administration of what are you talking about?
sentences.zh: 所以，特朗普政府实际上提出的抱怨之一是：你们到底在说什么？

sentences.en: Are you saying we've given illegal orders?
sentences.zh: 你们是说我们下达了非法命令吗？

sentences.en: Which ones?
sentences.zh: 具体是哪几条？

sentences.en: And, you know, it could be something about the fact that Trump has been deploying troops into cities, and some of them are acting kind of like police officers.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这可能与特朗普一直在向城市部署军队有关，其中一些军队的表现有点像警察。

sentences.en: It could be this boats operation.
sentences.zh: 也可能是指这次船只行动。

sentences.en: But the Trump administration responds very fiercely to that video and calls them insurrectionists and opens investigations of them for daring to say this thing,
sentences.zh: 但特朗普政府对该视频反应非常激烈，称他们为叛乱分子，并因为他们敢于说出这些话而对他们展开调查，

sentences.en: which is actually just illegal truism.
sentences.zh: 而这些话实际上只是法律上的老生常谈。

sentences.en: And that, I think, is a contributing factor to why, as the country's attention is returned to legal controversies surrounding Trump's killing of people on these boats,
sentences.zh: 我认为，这也是为什么当全国的注意力重新回到围绕特朗普在这些船只上杀人事件的法律争议时，

sentences.en: the reaction has been more fierce now than in September when it was still kind of a new thing that people were trying to wrap their heads around.
sentences.zh: 现在的反应比九月份时更为激烈，当时这还是一件人们试图理解的新鲜事。

sentences.en: This legal cloud has been apparent since early September, and Congress, controlled by the Republican Party,
sentences.zh: 这种法律阴云自九月初以来就一直存在，而由共和党控制的国会，

sentences.en: has not been particularly interested in performing much oversight until now.
sentences.zh: 直到现在才对进行监督表现出特别的兴趣。

sentences.en: And so as this effort unfolds in coming days and weeks, it will be interesting to see how broad the focus is, what questions lawmakers ask,
sentences.zh: 因此，随着这项工作在未来几天和几周内展开，看看他们的关注范围有多广、议员们会提出什么问题，

sentences.en: and what information they're able to extract.
sentences.zh: 以及他们能够获取什么信息，将会非常有趣。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: I'm Wena Liu.
sentences.zh: 我是 Wena Liu。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times games, and I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我负责编写《纽约时报》游戏中的《Connections》谜题，我热爱恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog, and I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗，也喜欢试图捉弄你们。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Mazursky, and I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我是 Sam Mazursky，我每天负责制作《Spelling Bee》和《Letterboxd》游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫做“联觉”的东西。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 我在听音乐时能看到颜色。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由像你们刚才听到的人那样的人制作的。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 请访问 nytimes.com/games 开始游戏。

sentences.en: Charlie, before the break, you told us about these congressional calls for investigation.
sentences.zh: Charlie，在休息之前，你告诉我们国会呼吁进行调查的事。

sentences.en: What might that look like if it happened?
sentences.zh: 如果真的发生了，那会是什么样子？

sentences.en: And what power does Congress actually have here?
sentences.zh: 国会在这里到底有什么权力？

sentences.en: So, now that some Republicans on the Armed Services Committees appear to be interested in getting some answers, at least about this second missile strike in this first attack,
sentences.zh: 现在，武装部队委员会的一些共和党人似乎有兴趣获得一些答案，至少是关于第一次袭击中第二次导弹打击的答案，

sentences.en: Congress is therefore awakening.
sentences.zh: 因此，国会正在觉醒。

sentences.en: We do not know at this stage how far this oversight effort will go.
sentences.zh: 我们目前还不知道这项监督工作会走多远。

sentences.en: It could be very searching.
sentences.zh: 它可能非常深入。

sentences.en: It could be very limited.
sentences.zh: 也可能非常有限。

sentences.en: And all that is going to depend on the appetite of Republicans to make life uncomfortable for the Trump administration, which, as any observer of politics knows,
sentences.zh: 这一切都将取决于共和党人让特朗普政府感到难堪的意愿，正如任何政治观察家所知，

sentences.en: is not something that is easy for them to do.
sentences.zh: 这对他们来说并非易事。

sentences.en: If they really want to get to the bottom of this, they have a number of things they can ask for and demand and push the limits to try to get.
sentences.zh: 如果他们真的想查个水落石出，他们可以要求、强求并推动极限去尝试获取很多东西。

sentences.en: Such as?
sentences.zh: 比如什么？

sentences.en: They can call witnesses and have them give sworn testimony.
sentences.zh: 他们可以传唤证人，让他们进行宣誓作证。

sentences.en: Hegseth, obviously.
sentences.zh: 显然是 Hegseth。

sentences.en: Admiral Bradley, obviously.
sentences.zh: 显然是 Bradley 上将。

sentences.en: There are things they could ask for as well.
sentences.zh: 他们也可以要求提供其他东西。

sentences.en: The administration has released, as we know, this sort of 30-second edited surveillance clip that doesn't show the follow-up strikes.
sentences.zh: 正如我们所知，政府发布了一段 30 秒的剪辑监控视频，其中没有显示后续的打击。

sentences.en: It doesn't show people surviving the first attack.
sentences.zh: 它没有显示第一次袭击后的幸存者。

sentences.en: But you know they've got that video.
sentences.zh: 但你知道他们有那段视频。

sentences.en: In fact, the New York Times has filed a lawsuit for the unedited video of that strike.
sentences.zh: 事实上，《纽约时报》已经就那次打击的未剪辑视频提起了诉讼。

sentences.en: Congress also could demand that video.
sentences.zh: 国会也可以要求提供那段视频。

sentences.en: A retired, very senior
sentences.zh: 一位退休的资深

sentences.en: JAG told me that one of the questions that could maybe be parsed through actual evidence is what kind of missile was it that was fired at the boat the second time?
sentences.zh: 军法署（JAG）官员告诉我，可以通过实际证据解析的问题之一是，第二次向船只发射的是什么类型的导弹？

sentences.en: Because they can be configured to be anti-personnel or anti-material.
sentences.zh: 因为它们可以配置为杀伤人员或摧毁物资。

sentences.en: Anti-personnel missile can produce a lot of shrapnel to try to kill people, as opposed to one that's trying to produce a big hole in a large object.
sentences.zh: 杀伤人员导弹可以产生大量弹片来杀伤人员，而不是那种试图在大物体上炸出一个大洞的导弹。

sentences.en: So, which kind did they shoot?
sentences.zh: 那么，他们发射的是哪一种？

sentences.en: And did they have the other kind available?
sentences.zh: 他们当时是否有另一种可供选择？

sentences.en: These are all the kinds of sort of evidentiary questions that if you're really drilling down into the
sentences.zh: 这些都是那种证据层面的问题，如果你真的深入挖掘

sentences.en: nuances of these nitty-gritty things of what was said and done at each moment, what was the intent
sentences.zh: 这些细枝末节的细微差别，即每一刻说了什么、做了什么，意图是什么，

sentences.en: what was the understanding, Congress could demand and then see if the Trump administration is willing to turn over.
sentences.zh: 理解是什么，国会可以提出要求，然后看看特朗普政府是否愿意交出。

sentences.en: I just want to understand what these investigations could even amount to.
sentences.zh: 我只是想了解这些调查到底能起到什么作用。

sentences.en: So hypothetically, if Congress determines that the military broke the law, what then?
sentences.zh: 假设国会认定军方违反了法律，那会怎样？

sentences.en: So obviously Congress itself is a political body and it performs oversight and it appropriates funds and it passes laws.
sentences.zh: 显然，国会本身是一个政治机构，它履行监督职能、拨款并制定法律。

sentences.en: It doesn't prosecute people.
sentences.zh: 它不负责起诉他人。

sentences.en: So it's not its job to bring charges against anyone.
sentences.zh: 所以，对任何人提起指控并不是它的工作。

sentences.en: It could cut off funds to the military for further boat strikes if it had the political will, meaning majority votes, to do that in future appropriations bills.
sentences.zh: 如果它有政治意愿，即在未来的拨款法案中获得多数票，它可以切断军方进行进一步船只打击的资金。

sentences.en: It could refuse to confirm Trump appointees until the administration stops doing this thing it hypothetically thinks it ought to stop doing.
sentences.zh: 它可以拒绝确认特朗普的任命人选，直到政府停止做它假设认为应该停止的事情。

sentences.en: You know, ultimately, in theory, it could impeach
sentences.zh: 你知道，从理论上讲，它最终可以弹劾

sentences.en: Trump and remove him from office.
sentences.zh: 特朗普并将他免职。

sentences.en: But we all know as a matter of political reality that that's unlikely to happen.
sentences.zh: 但我们都知道，从政治现实来看，这不太可能发生。

sentences.en: Even if Democrats retake control of one or both chambers, they won't have the two-thirds necessary to convict in the Senate.
sentences.zh: 即使民主党重新夺回一个或两个议院的控制权，他们也不会有参议院定罪所需的三分之二多数票。

sentences.en: Well, what about that DOJ memo that we were talking about, though?
sentences.zh: 那么，我们刚才谈到的司法部备忘录呢？

sentences.en: Like, if the military broke the law, but they didn't go outside of the bounds of what that memo authorized.
sentences.zh: 比如，如果军方违反了法律，但他们没有超出该备忘录授权的范围。

sentences.en: Is anybody vulnerable to any consequences?
sentences.zh: 有人会受到任何后果吗？

sentences.en: So what you're asking about now is if someone broke the law here, whether it's the entire
sentences.zh: 你现在问的是，如果有人在这里违法了，无论是整个

sentences.en: operation or just this follow-up missile strike, is there a place where theoretically someone could be charged, let's say, with murder or a war crime down the road?
sentences.zh: 行动还是仅仅是这次后续的导弹打击，在理论上是否有一个地方可以起诉某人，比如未来以谋杀或战争罪起诉？

sentences.en: And the answer to that is it's very difficult to see where that could happen.
sentences.zh: 答案是，很难看出这种情况会发生。

sentences.en: The fact is that right now, while these actions are happening, the Justice Department's official position is this is lawful
sentences.zh: 事实是，现在当这些行动发生时，司法部的官方立场是这是合法的，

sentences.en: and that you can't prosecute someone just for doing a thing that you yourself, that is the Justice Department, said was lawful at the time.
sentences.zh: 而且你不能仅仅因为某人做了你本人——也就是司法部——当时说合法的事情就起诉他。

sentences.en: They're relying on your assurances.
sentences.zh: 他们依赖于你的保证。

sentences.en: You can't bait and switch people.
sentences.zh: 你不能欺骗和误导人们。

sentences.en: This is a matter of due process.
sentences.zh: 这是一个正当程序问题。

sentences.en: And so this OLC memo, the Justice Department memo,
sentences.zh: 所以这份法律顾问办公室（OLC）的备忘录，即司法部备忘录，

sentences.en: Now, a former head of OLC who teaches at Harvard now named Jack Goldsmith has famously called them get out of jail free cards.
sentences.zh: 现在，一位曾在哈佛任教的前 OLC 主管 Jack Goldsmith 曾著名地称它们为“免罪金牌”。

sentences.en: Golden shields.
sentences.zh: 黄金盾牌。

sentences.en: You can just write down some nonsense on a piece of paper on OLC letterhead, and suddenly people are free to do whatever that memo says.
sentences.zh: 你可以在 OLC 信笺上写下一些废话，突然之间，人们就可以自由地做那份备忘录所说的任何事情。

sentences.en: And there's just not really a check on that.
sentences.zh: 而且对此并没有真正的制衡。

sentences.en: It's just the way the system is structured.
sentences.zh: 这就是系统构建的方式。

sentences.en: I just want to pause here because what you're saying is kind of remarkable.
sentences.zh: 我只想在这里停一下，因为你所说的话非常引人注目。

sentences.en: I mean, you cannot write a contract, for instance, and have two parties sign it that breaks the law and say, well, we have a contract.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你不能写一份合同，让双方签署一份违法的合同，然后说，好吧，我们有合同。

sentences.en: What you are saying is that if the DOJ writes a memo and says that something is lawful, that protects anybody carrying out orders within the bounds of that memo,
sentences.zh: 你的意思是，如果司法部写了一份备忘录说某事是合法的，那么它就能保护任何在备忘录范围内执行命令的人，

sentences.en: even if by any other analysis, those actions are determined to be illegal.
sentences.zh: 即使通过任何其他分析，这些行为被认定为非法。

sentences.en: Just the fact that that memo exists, it sounds like protects people from prosecution.
sentences.zh: 仅仅因为那份备忘录的存在，听起来就能保护人们免受起诉。

sentences.en: Domestic federal prosecution.
sentences.zh: 国内联邦层面的起诉。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: This is the power of the Office of Legal Counsel within the Justice Department.
sentences.zh: 这就是司法部内法律顾问办公室的权力。

sentences.en: And we saw an earlier round of this 20 years ago when after 9-11, the Bush administration had in its Office of Legal Counsel a lawyer named John Yoo
sentences.zh: 我们在 20 年前看到了这一轮的早期版本，当时在 9/11 事件后，布什政府的法律顾问办公室里有一位名叫 John Yoo 的律师，

sentences.en: who had an idiosyncratically broad view of executive power that most people thought was wrong.
sentences.zh: 他对行政权力的看法极其宽泛，大多数人都认为这是错误的。

sentences.en: And under his view, the president could authorize anything he thought was necessary to protect national security, things like wiretapping without warrants, torturing prisoners.
sentences.zh: 根据他的观点，总统可以授权他认为保护国家安全所必需的任何事情，比如未经授权的窃听、折磨囚犯。

sentences.en: These memos are later rescinded, but they were there while this stuff was happening.
sentences.zh: 这些备忘录后来被撤销了，但在这些事情发生时它们确实存在。

sentences.en: And when Eric Holder, the liberal attorney general under Barack Obama, comes in in 2009 and opens a criminal investigation into the treatment of
sentences.zh: 当巴拉克·奥巴马政府下的自由派司法部长 Eric Holder 在 2009 年上任并对中情局在布什政府下对待

sentences.en: detainees by the CIA under the Bush administration, because of this problem of the OLC's assurances
sentences.zh: 被拘留者的情况展开刑事调查时，由于 OLC 当时保证的问题，

sentences.en: at the time, he says, we are only going to look at actions that went beyond the guidance that was blessed by the OLC.
sentences.zh: 他说，我们只会调查那些超出了 OLC 认可的指导方针的行为。

sentences.en: So the OLC said you can waterboard people and you waterboarded people, even if everyone else says drowning people is torture and it's illegal, the OLC said it was okay.
sentences.zh: 所以 OLC 说你可以对人进行水刑，你就对人进行了水刑，即使其他人说淹死人是酷刑且是非法的，但 OLC 说没问题。

sentences.en: We're not going to prosecute you for that.
sentences.zh: 我们不会因为那个起诉你。

sentences.en: Now, the catch, of course, and this is where we circle back to this conversation about the second strike, is the memo says, apparently,
sentences.zh: 当然，问题在于——这也是我们回到关于第二次打击的对话的地方——备忘录显然说，

sentences.en: because this is supposedly an armed conflict, strikes that comport with the law of war, the law of armed conflict, are permissible.
sentences.zh: 因为这被认为是武装冲突，符合战争法、武装冲突法的打击是允许的。

sentences.en: The second missile strike in the first attack, which kills the shipwrecked survivors of the first missile strike arguably does not comport with the law of armed conflict.
sentences.zh: 第一次袭击中的第二次导弹打击，杀死了第一次导弹打击后的船难幸存者，可以说是不符合武装冲突法的。

sentences.en: And so that's one place where this particular strike, as opposed to all the others, might be more vulnerable to later legal scrutiny because especially if there's evidence
sentences.zh: 所以，这是这次特定打击——与其他打击不同——可能更容易受到后续法律审查的一个地方，特别是如果有证据表明

sentences.en: that Admiral Bradley's specific intent was to target the still-living crew members as opposed to the boat or the supposed cargo.
sentences.zh: Bradley 上将的具体意图是针对仍然活着的船员，而不是船只或所谓的货物。

sentences.en: That's a point where, despite the OLC memo, you could see a later prosecutor, I guess this would be in the court-martial system, were there the political will to do so,
sentences.zh: 这是一个尽管有 OLC 备忘录，你仍可以看到后来的检察官——我想这会在军事法庭系统中——如果有政治意愿的话，

sentences.en: taking a hard look at that.
sentences.zh: 会对此进行严格审查。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Basically, if the intent was to kill the survivors of that first strike, it arguably would be outside the bounds of that memo
sentences.zh: 基本上，如果意图是杀死第一次打击的幸存者，那可以说是在该备忘录的范围之外，

sentences.en: and outside the bounds of what is considered legal warfare.
sentences.zh: 也在被视为合法战争的范围之外。

sentences.en: So therefore, the people who launched that strike potentially could be prosecuted.
sentences.zh: 因此，发动那次打击的人可能会被起诉。

sentences.en: Potentially, down the road, if there's no sweeping, preemptive pardon.
sentences.zh: 如果没有任何全面的、先发制人的赦免，未来可能会被起诉。

sentences.en: Now, of course, there's also international law.
sentences.zh: 当然，还有国际法。

sentences.en: There is a court in The Hague, in the Netherlands, called the International Criminal Court.
sentences.zh: 在荷兰海牙有一个法院，叫做国际刑事法院。

sentences.en: And it exists as a standing court to prosecute war crimes, crimes against humanity, genocide.
sentences.zh: 它作为一个常设法院存在，旨在起诉战争罪、危害人类罪和种族灭绝罪。

sentences.en: And I should note that we are not a party to the International Criminal Court.
sentences.zh: 我应该指出，我们不是国际刑事法院的缔约国。

sentences.en: We are not a party.
sentences.zh: 我们不是缔约国。

sentences.en: The countries of Venezuela and Colombia, among others, are parties.
sentences.zh: 委内瑞拉和哥伦比亚等国是缔约国。

sentences.en: And so there are circumstances in which, in theory, American officials could be prosecuted in The
sentences.zh: 因此，在理论上，美国官员可能会在海牙因在委内瑞拉境内对委内瑞拉人采取的行动而被起诉。

sentences.en: Hague for actions, let's say, inside Venezuela, against Venezuelans.
sentences.zh: 同样地，现在，

sentences.zh: 海牙法院对弗拉基米尔·普京发出了逮捕令，尽管俄罗斯不是创建该法院的条约的成员国，

sentences.zh: 这是因为他在乌克兰的行动，而乌克兰是成员国。

sentences.en: for his actions in Ukraine, because Ukraine is a member.
sentences.zh: 但这些船只袭击目前至少都发生在国际水域。

sentences.zh: 它们没有在委内瑞拉或哥伦比亚注册。

sentences.en: They're not registered to Venezuela or Colombia.
sentences.zh: 它们只是小船。

sentences.en: They're just little boats.
sentences.zh: 它们不是大船。

sentences.en: They're not ships.
sentences.zh: 因此，由于没有在任何国家注册，也不在任何国家的领土内，国际刑事法院对这些袭击没有管辖权。

sentences.en: And so without being registered to a country, without being in the country's territory, there's no jurisdiction for the International Criminal Court over these attacks.
sentences.zh: 所以目前什么都没有，除非这次行动蔓延到委内瑞拉（可能会发生），但就目前而言，关于这些袭击（包括 9 月 2 日的袭击），

sentences.en: So nothing for now, unless this operation spreads to Venezuela, as it might, but for now, nothing on these attacks, including the September 2 attack,
sentences.zh: 都不会提交给国际刑事法院。

sentences.en: would come before the International Criminal Court.
sentences.zh: Charlie，我们今天的谈话是由我们讨论的关于第一艘船第二次打击的更多审查，以及这是否违反武装冲突规则所引发的。

sentences.en: Charlie, our conversation today was prompted by, as we discussed, more scrutiny about the second strike on that first boat and whether that violates the rules of armed conflict.
sentences.zh: 但我们的谈话并不是由关于向这些船只开火的整个行动是否非法的问题引发的，对吧？

sentences.zh: 我很好奇，作为一个一直关注这个故事每一个转折的国家安全专家，

sentences.en: We'll see how committed they remain to, you know, getting the answers.
sentences.zh: 但这看起来有点像国会监督应该发挥作用的方式。

sentences.en: But it looks kind of like the way congressional oversight is supposed to function.

sentences.zh: 另一方面，关于谁在什么时候说了什么、意图是什么的问题，

sentences.zh: 这确实是国会监督的核心。

sentences.en: and with what interpretation about the second strike are very narrow once you start really drilling down on it.
sentences.zh: 一旦你开始深入挖掘，关于第二次打击的解读就变得非常狭隘了。

sentences.en: in a way that is arguably distracting from the broader issue that has been apparent from the beginning
sentences.zh: 这在某种程度上可以说转移了人们对从一开始就显而易见的更广泛问题的关注，

sentences.en: and is not limited to the second missile strike, but to all the missile strikes.
sentences.zh: 而且这不仅限于第二次导弹袭击，而是涉及所有的导弹袭击。

sentences.en: The United States is engaged in an extraordinary, legally edgy to say the least, operation with literally deadly consequences and the broader issue of is this an armed conflict
sentences.zh: 美国正在进行一场非同寻常、至少可以说在法律上处于边缘的行动，并造成了实实在在的致命后果，而更广泛的问题是，这是否属于武装冲突，

sentences.en: is this a war at all hangs over the entire thing and if it's not a war if it's not an armed conflict

sentences.zh: 目前已经发生了21次船只袭击。

sentences.zh: 83人丧生。

sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，布拉德利海军上将做出了正确的决定，最终击沉了那艘船并消除了威胁。

sentences.en: The result is a boon in the short term for President Trump and the Republican Party, which had worried that its narrow House majority would grow even slimmer.
